threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will come when it says on the screen. The real London timing has a mind of its own, mate.
Caught a night bus from Brixton the other week; a guy argued with the driver over the last donut from a nearby kebab shop.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw someone using a bike as a stroller for their dog outside the Späti at 2 AM. That’s classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do people celebrate a bus strike with picnics on the roads, making the most of transit chaos like it’s a public holiday.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re from the Mission when you can spot a tourist by their confused expression at the BART delays. They think it’s just a bad day.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy with a full keyboard on a Muni bus, playing tunes to a captive crowd. Only in SF does that feel like a regular Tuesday.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell but miss the real charm of Gràcia's hidden squares, where locals sip vermut and chat for hours, completely overlooked.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re still trying to make sense of the metro map—look for the ones squinting and flipping it upside down at the station.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still get flustered trying to navigate the bus map and miss the fact that the 394 ends at midnight, not the 24-hour routes.
Heard a couple arguing about whether the 333 bus driver took the scenic route. Turns out, the driver’s just a real fan of the backstreets.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy in a tracksuit debating philosophy with a pigeon on Karl-Marx-Straße. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find spontaneous street art battles that turn an ordinary day into a canvas. Graffiti artists push creativity to its limits.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they can name the taco truck behind the laundromat but still can’t figure out BART delays on a Friday.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading commuters with a ukulele on the 38 bus today, while someone else tried to sell him a sandwich. Only in SF...

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is all about the parks and plazas, but they miss the tucked-away bakeries serving the best panellets at dawn.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they stare at the metro map like it’s hieroglyphics, while locals glide through without a second thought.
